name: loopcom
title: LOOPCOM Veo 3 Video Profile
description: Yiddish-to-English call and voicemail translation. Telecom SaaS, WhatsApp-status-first vertical advertising, assembled into 15-30s spots.

safeZone.note: WhatsApp overlays the sender row at the top and the reply bar at the bottom, and some devices clip the extremes. Keep every load-bearing element inside the middle 73% of the frame.

assembly.method: Chain clips by feeding the approved final frame of one shot in as the first frame of the next, so the spot flows instead of jump-cutting.

typography.note: Copy ships in both Hebrew script and Latin depending on audience, so every render must stay language-neutral. Build one visual master and lay two text versions over it rather than rendering twice.

audio.caveat: Each clip generates its own audio independently. In a chained 15-30s spot the music will restart and jump at every seam, so replace the bed with one continuous track in post and keep Veo's effects.

logo.note: Veo never renders the LOOPCOM mark, a wordmark, or anything that reads as a brand emblem. The logo is composited onto the assembled spot, so the final clip of a chain must resolve to a calm centred composition with clean space for it.

styleSuffix: Shoot it like a commercial: long-lens perspective, shallow depth of field, volumetric light, physically plausible glass and refraction, rich blacks, controlled highlights and weighted easing on every move. Favour one idea rendered beautifully over a sequence of events. Deep navy-black environment with premium glass, precise cyan edge lighting, restrained glow, generous negative space and fine suspended particles. Colors limited to mint #5EEAD4, teal #14B8A6, technology blue #0EA5E9, white and navy-black #020A12, with no other hues. One continuous composition, very slow push-in, stable camera: no cuts, shake, rotation or extreme zoom. Nothing is ever completely still, so particles drift and light breathes and no element freezes. No people and no live-action. The frame carries no text or branding at all: no words, letters, numbers, captions, labels, logos, wordmarks or emblems, because copy and the brand mark are composited afterwards in either Hebrew or Latin. Keep the composition symmetric with key motion inside the middle three quarters, and hold the lower third calm for type. Audio: instrumental only and free of voices, a futuristic electronic pulse with sub-bass and precise interface sounds.
rules: Veo renders no words, ever. Typography and the logo are composited in the editor.
Prefer one idea rendered beautifully over a checklist of icon events. Literal UI symbols read as clip art; material, light and depth read as a brand film.
Typography is composited in post, never rendered by Veo. Hebrew script especially, which Veo renders badly.
The LOOPCOM mark is composited onto the finished spot, never rendered. End a chain on a calm centred frame so the logo has somewhere clean to land.
Every render must read the same under Hebrew and Latin copy. One visual master, two text versions, one render cost.
Keep load-bearing motion inside the middle 73% of the frame. WhatsApp covers the top and bottom.
Draft on the lite tier, approve the composition, then render once on the final tier.
Hold a seed across iterations so a prompt edit reads as a real change.
Chain a multi-clip spot by first frame, and reuse the seed across the chain to keep the look stable.
Veo audio is kept, but replace the music bed in post on any spot longer than one clip.
No people. The brand language excludes them, and the market this serves commonly avoids depicting people in advertising.
Nothing sits still. Keep every element drifting or breathing. On text shots the word moves as one block; letterforms never animate individually, which is where morphing starts.
No negative prompts. Every exclusion is stated in the prompt itself, which keeps one instruction channel instead of two and lets any tier render a draft.

Keep the shot description under about 130 words. Stating exclusions in the prompt rather than a negative prompt costs roughly 40 words, so a resolved prompt lands near 300 against the 616-word original.
Typography is composited in post. This is now an evidence-based rule, not a preference: rendered text is 0 for 3 on this project at a cost of $7.20, while non-text shots are 2 for 2 at $0.40.
Put a word that must survive at the start or the end of the clip. Both failures hit the mid-clip beat.
Never block on a generation call. Start it, record the operation name, then poll.

with-text.styleSuffix: Visual language: a premium telecommunications interface in deep navy-black. Glass surfaces, cyan edge lighting, restrained glow, thin circuit paths, generous negative space, subtle particles, polished commercial motion design. Colors limited to mint #5EEAD4, teal #14B8A6, technology blue #0EA5E9, white and navy-black #020A12, with no other hues. One continuous composition, very slow push-in, stable camera: no cuts, shake, rotation or extreme zoom. Nothing is ever completely still, so particles drift and light breathes and no element freezes. Keep the frame clean, free of flicker and duplicated icons. No people and no live-action. Typography is clean bold uppercase geometric sans-serif in white with a restrained cyan glow, in Latin letters only. Render only the words named in the shot, each appearing exactly once and spelled exactly as written. Words drift and pulse as whole blocks while their letterforms stay rigid and sharp, never morphing, duplicating or flickering. No other text and no branding anywhere: no captions, labels, logos, wordmarks or emblems. Keep text inside the middle three quarters. Audio: instrumental only and free of voices, with sub-bass and precise interface sounds.
with-text.note: For shots where Veo renders the words itself. Exclusions live in the prompt, not a negative prompt, so the lite tier can be used for drafts.
with-text.record: 0 usable outputs from 3 attempts, $7.20 spent. Not approved for client deliverables.
with-text.retiredReason: Retired 2026-08-28. Typography is composited in post. Kept for the record: 0 usable outputs from 3 attempts at $7.20, failing once by omission and once as ENGDISH.

evidence.note: Observed on this project, not vendor documentation. Update it as the record grows; the ledger only covers renders made after journaling was added.

renders.outcome: lost to a 60s client timeout before the operation name was recorded
ENGLISH absent; YIDDISH and LOOPCOM rendered

withRenderedText.note: Three attempts, no usable output at any price.

textFindings: Two of two multi-word shots failed, and both failed on the same word: ENGLISH, the third word and the mid-clip beat. Position looks like the risk factor, not the word.
Two distinct failure modes. Without blur direction the word was omitted entirely. With blur and glow on the type it was malformed into ENGDISH.
Blur and bloom on typography are a direct cause of malformed letterforms. Defocus softens the stroke junction that separates an L from a D.
A misspelling guard in the negative prompt was active during the ENGDISH render and did not prevent it. Guards discourage, they do not enforce.
Shortening the prompt from 616 to 309 words changed the failure mode but did not remove it.
nonTextFindings: Two of two abstract shots with no rendered text were usable on the first attempt, on the cheapest tier.

apiConstraints: The lite tier rejects negativePrompt with HTTP 400 rather than ignoring it.
personGeneration 'dont_allow' is not supported and returns HTTP 400. Exclude people in the prompt instead.
An MCP tool call times out at 60s while an 8s render takes 61 to 91s. Always start the operation and poll; never block on a single call.
A timed-out call still bills. Record the operation name before waiting, then recover it rather than re-rendering.

textPolicy.rule: Veo never renders words. All typography, in Hebrew script or Latin, is composited in the editor along with the logo.
rationale: Rendered text is 0 usable from 3 attempts at $7.20; non-text shots are 2 from 2 at $0.40.
Veo has no font renderer, so a correctly spelled take is a lucky draw rather than a solved problem. Every render would need its spelling re-checked forever.
A post pass already happens on every finished spot to add the logo, so the words cost nothing extra there.
One language-neutral master serves both the Hebrew and Latin cuts instead of rolling separately for each.
